## Summary

I diagnosed and verified the bug. There was no existing repo on this machine (only `/workspace/problem.json`), so I built a self-contained fixture and validated the git semantics directly.

**Root cause:** After `--`, git parses **everything as a pathspec**. So `git diff --quiet -- apps packages ':(exclude)…' "$range"` silently discards the revision range as a non-matching path and falls back to comparing **worktree vs. index**. The verdict is then driven by unrelated working-tree dirt — a dirty post-build tree yields exit 1 on every call → always-stale. On a clean tree the same bug yields a silent false-FRESH, which is why it evaded detection.

**Verified three-probe matrix (git 2.53.0):**

| Probe | `range -- paths` (correct) | `-- paths range` (buggy) |
|---|---|---|
| A: board-only range, clean | 0 fresh | 0 fresh |
| B: in-range `apps/` change, clean | 1 stale | **0 false-fresh** |
| C: board-only range, post-build dirty | 0 fresh | **1 always-stale** |

The smoking gun: `git diff --name-only -- apps packages HEAD~1..HEAD` prints `apps/app.txt` from the worktree even though the range contains no `apps/` change.

**Exact fix** (move range before `--` in the `execFileSync` arg array):
```js
execFileSync('git', ['diff', '--quiet', range, '--', 'apps', 'packages', ':(exclude)board/**'], …)
```
Plus hardening to distinguish git exit `1` (diff) from `>1` (real error, throw instead of mislabeling stale).

**Deliverables:**
- `/workspace/solution.md` (and copy at `~/solution.md`) — full analysis, fix, hardening, verification, CI regression assertion.
- `/workspace/repro-range-after-separator.sh` (and `~/…`) — runnable fixture, exits 0 to confirm the bug; re-run output included above.

All claims in the document were executed and verified, including the hardened `rangeTouchesGatedPaths` function (correctly throws `status=128` for a bogus range rather than reporting stale).
